introduction: This foundational level introduces the 'Hidden Disabilities'. It distinguishes Specific Learning Disabilities (SLDs) from Intellectual Disabilities (ID), establishes the core definitions of the 'Dys-' family of disorders, and outlines the basic traits of ADHD and Autism.

core_concepts.title: What is a Specific Learning Disability (SLD)?
core_concepts.description:
An SLD is a neurological disorder that affects the brain's ability to receive, process, store, or respond to information. 
Core Rule: Children with SLDs have AVERAGE or ABOVE-AVERAGE intelligence (Normal IQ). Their disability is a gap between their actual potential and their academic achievement. 
SLDs are NOT caused by intellectual disability, visual/hearing impairments, lack of education, or poor economic background.

core_concepts.title: The 'Dys' Family of Disabilities
core_concepts.description:
1. Dyslexia: A language-based reading disability. Characterized by difficulty in phonological awareness, decoding words, reading fluency, and spelling. (e.g., confusing 'b' and 'd', or reading 'saw' as 'was').
2. Dysgraphia: A writing disability. Poor handwriting, difficulty organizing thoughts on paper, extremely poor spatial planning on the page.
3. Dyscalculia: A mathematical disability. Difficulty understanding number concepts (number sense), memorizing math facts, and performing calculations.
4. Dyspraxia: A motor-coordination disability (Developmental Coordination Disorder). Clumsiness, difficulty with fine motor tasks (typing, tying shoelaces) and gross motor tasks (catching a ball).

core_concepts.title: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
core_concepts.description:
A neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by an ongoing pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning.
- Inattention: Wandering off task, lacking persistence, difficulty sustaining focus, being highly disorganized.
- Hyperactivity: Excessive motor activity when it is not appropriate (excessive fidgeting, tapping, or talkativeness).
- Impulsivity: Hasty actions occurring in the moment without forethought (blurting out answers, interrupting others).

core_concepts.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
core_concepts.description:
A complex developmental condition that involves persistent challenges in social interaction, speech and nonverbal communication, and restricted/repetitive behaviors.
It is a 'Spectrum' because the abilities and needs of people with ASD vary immensely—from highly gifted and independent to severely challenged and needing full-time care.

important_entities.name: Dysphasia vs. Aphasia
important_entities.key_fact: Language disorders affecting communication, not just reading.
important_entities.significance: Aphasia is the total or partial loss of the ability to communicate, usually caused by brain injury or stroke. Dysphasia is a partial impairment of language (difficulty speaking or comprehending spoken words). Do not confuse these with Dyslexia, which is specifically a reading/decoding issue.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a child writes 'b' instead of 'd', parents often think the child needs glasses. Examiners test this misconception. Dyslexia is a NEUROLOGICAL processing issue, not an optical (vision) issue. Glasses will not cure dyslexia; multisensory structured language education will.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Lexia = Words, Graphia = Writing, Calculia = Math, Praxia = Practice/Movement
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Identify the disability instantly by translating the Greek/Latin root word.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a question asks to identify a child who 'can orally explain a brilliant story but produces a totally illegible, poorly structured written paragraph,' the answer is strictly **Dysgraphia**.
